findings.section: Design — Failure paths in the tick
findings.title: Failure handling forks on reviewer count
findings.detail: With one reviewer any `res.error` parks `open_failed`/`config_invalid` campaign-wide (rule 1). With two or more, the same error becomes a per-persona `missing` result plus a retry (rules 3-4). So adding a second reviewer silently changes how a transient runner error behaves, and the spec says nothing about whether SPEC-0205/0202 will keep the split or unify it. This is workable, and the test plan covers both sides. Add one sentence to Open questions or Non-goals saying the divergence is deliberate and interim.

findings.title: Escalation detail text for the single-reviewer wrapper
findings.detail: `decide_review` currently parks with the detail 'the conformance reviewer returned no usable verdict twice'. The spec says the park 'names the personas'. State whether the `decide_review` wrapper keeps the old string verbatim, because AC8 requires SPEC-0187 behaviour to be unchanged. If any existing test or doc matches that string, say which.

findings.title: Interrupted pass with every verdict already valid
findings.detail: Valid verdicts are stored with the current `loop` on an interrupted pass. If all reviewers were valid, `plan_step` finds nothing pending, returns the full list, and re-runs every reviewer. That is accepted in the spec, but it throws away stored verdicts and costs a full extra budget. It is cheaper to treat the aggregate as complete and run the decision. The current wording is internally consistent, so this is optional.

findings.title: Pool sizing changes concurrency beyond slots
findings.detail: The pool becomes `max(slots, all pending_agent entries)`, so gate and implementer tasks are no longer throttled by `slots` either. The spec argues this is bounded by admission, which is fine. A test asserting that non-review ticks never exceed `slots` would pin it down, and AC3a only covers the reviewer case.

findings.title: Dense ACs
findings.detail: AC3b and AC6 each bundle five or more independently testable rules. The test plan lists them separately, so the implementer is covered. Splitting them would help the done-checklist. There are 9 ACs in all, which is within size limits.

findings.title: Legacy int semantics
findings.detail: `review_retries` is 'retry passes used', while `review_retries_by_persona` counts per persona. When A and B are both missing, the int goes up by 1 and each per-persona counter by 1. A one-line example would remove any doubt.
